args.name: IDX $100 Minimum Payoff 3x Upside Note - 4Q
args.description: Maturity in 4 quarters (1 year). You pay $102.50 per note. At maturity you receive, in dollars per note: 100 + 300 * max(0, IDX/IDX0 - 1), where IDX0 is IDX on the issue date and IDX is IDX at maturity. Minimum payoff is $100 if IDX is flat or falls, so in that case you lose $2.50 versus the purchase price (about 2.44%). This $100 minimum is NOT protection of the $102.50 purchase price. Breakeven requires an IDX rise of about 0.83%: payoff exceeds $102.50 only above that. Examples: IDX flat/down, payoff $100, loss $2.50; IDX +1%, payoff $103, gain $0.50; IDX +5%, payoff $115, gain $12.50. No coupons, no cap in the formula, no knock-in and no downside leverage; payoff depends only on diversified IDX, not on single names B or C or on OIL. Bank pricing model at issue: model value $101.75, so the $102.50 issue price is $0.75 (about 0.74%) above model value; that difference is the bank's markup/profit per note before hedging costs. Model outcomes: 5th percentile payoff $100, median payoff $100 (so a $2.50 loss versus purchase price is the median model outcome), 99th percentile payoff $110.34, and model chance of payoff below $100 is 0%. Past model chance of any loss versus the purchase price for this same structure was about 72%. Upside is not guaranteed and IDX performance is uncertain.
args.rationale: Keep the simple, transparent IDX-only structure that sold 72 notes at a $0.25 markup and 65, 63 and 71 notes at a $0.75 markup in prior quarters. IDX is the diversified underlying, avoiding single-name concentration in B and C amid mixed/negative company headlines (including a regulator probe into B and B guidance cut) and avoiding OIL commodity exposure. The payoff retains a disclosed $100 minimum (not protection of the $102.50 purchase price), no knock-in or downside leverage, complexity remains low at 20, and model chance of payoff below $100 is 0% (p5 and median $100, 99th percentile $110.34). Keeping issue at $102.50 vs model $101.75 is a $0.75 markup under 1%, while explicitly disclosing model value, markup, median payoff, percentile outcomes, breakeven IDX rise of about 0.83%, and example gains/losses, making the trade-off clear and suitable as a fairly described retail note despite the disclosed chance of a $2.50 loss.
